units.source_text: 他对西方舞蹈的兴趣也是如此。

en.t: His interest in Western dance was like that as well.

units.source_text: 岛村生长在东京闹市区，从小熟悉歌舞伎，学生时代偏爱传统舞蹈和舞剧。

en.t: Shimamura had grown up in the busy downtown districts of Tokyo, had been familiar with kabuki since childhood, and in his student days had favored traditional dance and dance drama.

units.source_text: 他天性固执，只要摸上哪一门，就非要彻底学到手不可。

en.t: He was stubborn by nature, and once he touched a subject, he had to master it thoroughly.

units.source_text: 所以他广泛涉猎古代的记载，走访各流派的师傅，

en.t: So he read widely through old records and went around visiting masters of the various schools,

units.source_text: 后来还结识了日本舞蹈的新秀，甚至还写起研究和评论文章来。

en.t: and later he also came to know promising young figures in Japanese dance, even beginning to write research and critical essays.

units.source_text: 而且对传统日本舞蹈的停滞状态，以及对自以为是的新尝试，自然也感到强烈的不满。

en.t: Naturally, he also felt a strong dissatisfaction with the stagnation of traditional Japanese dance and with self-satisfied new experiments.

units.source_text: 一种急切的心情促使他思考：事态已经如此，自己除了投身到实际运动中去，别无他途。

en.t: An urgent feeling drove him to think that, things having reached this point, he had no path left but to throw himself into practical action.

units.source_text: 当受到年轻的日本舞蹈家的吸引时，他突然改行搞西方舞蹈，根本不去看日本舞蹈了。

en.t: When he was drawn in by young Japanese dancers, he suddenly changed course and took up Western dance, no longer going to see Japanese dance at all.

units.source_text: 相反地，他收集有关西方舞蹈的书籍和图片，甚至煞费苦心地从外国搞来海报和节目单之类的东西。

en.t: Instead, he collected books and photographs about Western dance, and even went to great pains to obtain posters, programs, and the like from abroad.

units.source_text: 这绝非仅仅出于对异国和未知境界的好奇。

en.t: This was by no means merely curiosity about foreign countries and unknown realms.

units.source_text: 在这里，他新发现的喜悦，就在于他没能亲眼看到西方人的舞蹈。

en.t: Here, the joy he newly discovered lay precisely in the fact that he could not see Westerners dance with his own eyes.

units.source_text: 从岛村向来不看日本人跳西方舞就足以证明这一点。

en.t: This was proved well enough by the fact that Shimamura never watched Japanese people perform Western dance.

units.source_text: 没有什么比凭借西方印刷品来写有关西方舞蹈的文章更轻松的了。

en.t: Nothing was easier than writing about Western dance on the basis of Western printed materials.

units.source_text: 描写没有看过的舞蹈，实属无稽之谈。

en.t: To describe dances one had never seen was truly absurd.

units.source_text: 再没有比这个更“纸上谈兵”的了。

en.t: Nothing could be more detached from practice than this.

units.source_text: 可是，那是天堂的诗。

en.t: And yet, it was the poetry of heaven.

units.source_text: 虽美其名曰研究，其实是任意想象，不是欣赏舞蹈家栩栩如生的肉体舞蹈艺术，

en.t: Though it was dignified with the name of research, it was in fact arbitrary imagination, not an appreciation of the living bodily art of dancers,

units.source_text: 而是欣赏他自己空想的舞蹈幻影，这种空想是由西方的文字和图片产生的，

en.t: but an appreciation of dancing phantoms of his own imagining, fantasies produced by Western words and pictures,

units.source_text: 仿佛憧憬那不曾见过的爱情一样。

en.t: as though he were yearning for a love he had never seen.

units.source_text: 因为他不时写些介绍西方舞蹈的文章，也勉强算是个文人墨客。

en.t: Because he occasionally wrote pieces introducing Western dance, he could just barely be counted as a man of letters.

units.source_text: 他虽以此自嘲，但对没有职业的他来说，有时也会得到一种心灵上的慰藉。

en.t: Although he mocked himself for it, for a man without an occupation it sometimes brought a kind of comfort to his heart.
